runs: In this module, we will define production and outline the main sectors of production. We will also define fundamental concepts such as: economies of scale, quality control and smart manufacturing. Particular attention will be dedicated to the relocation of business operations and on a special focus on circular economy.

QC involves activities such as inspection of products, testing them, making sure they meet certain requirements, maintained records of production processes, taking corrective actions when needed. For instance, in manufacturing testing is carried out at each phase of the production process, from the raw materials to the finished product.

Typical of Industry 4.0, where machines and production systems are interconnected, allowing companies to obtain real time information at any step of the production process. So, they can immediately react to changes in demand and conditions of the supply chain.
It is based on four elements: connectivity, data and computational power; Artificial Intelligence; Human-machine interaction; Advanced engineering.
thanks to IoT, connected machines can share data with other devices, but also store and immediately manage these data with cloud computing, thus optimising costs and time.

Reshoring can be done for several reasons:
: when production costs abroad increase, leading to lower savings than anticipated.
: when the company’s goal is to improve the quality of their goods and services, or to have more control over the production process.
: it reduces risks associated with offshoring (e.g. unstable international trade, management issues in the supply chain).
: there may be concerns about the protection of national security or intellectual property, especially in industries that are key to national defence.
